task: We finally closed on our first house and are hosting a housewarming on Sunday, December 7 from 2 to 5pm. Write a text-style invitation for our group chat that says it's a potluck, we'll provide drinks, and to bring slippers because we just refinished the floors.
rewrite:
ambition:     A pro host makes the potluck work by asking everyone to reply with what they're bringing. That keeps it from turning into six bags of chips. The invite should also make the slipper ask sound like part of the fun.
agency:       The best source is the group chat itself: how these friends actually text, and whether the address is already known to them. That isn't in reach, so assume a warm, casual tone and leave a blank for the address.
acceleration: Use standard group-text invite structure: a lead line with the news, then date and time on their own short lines, then the three asks (potluck, drinks on you, slippers), then a "reply with your dish" close. Keep it to a few short lines with one or two emoji at most.
accuracy:     Check the date against a calendar. December 7, 2026 falls on a Monday, not a Sunday (Sunday is December 6; December 7 was a Sunday in 2025), so confirm which one is right before sending. For tone, the closest outside check is whether it sounds like something you'd already send to that chat.

answers.plain:
We closed on the house! 🏡🔑

Come celebrate with us at our housewarming:

📅 Sunday, December 7
🕑 2–5pm

It's a potluck, so bring a dish to share. We'll have the drinks covered. 🥂

One request: please bring slippers or cozy socks. We just refinished the floors and want to keep them looking good. 🧦

Can't wait to show you the place! Let us know if you can make it. 💛
answers.nudge:
**Heads-up before you send:** in 2026, December 7 falls on a **Monday**. Sunday is December 6. I wrote the invite as you gave it, so check which one is right.

## Main invitation

> 🏡 WE GOT A HOUSE (and you're invited to it)
>
> Housewarming! Sunday, Dec 7, 2-5pm
> 📍 [address]
>
> Come see the new place, eat good food, and help us make it feel lived-in.
>
> 🍽️ It's a potluck, so bring a dish you love (a main, side, or dessert all work).
> 🍹 We've got the drinks covered.
> 🧦 Please bring slippers or cozy socks. We just refinished the floors and want to keep them looking good for at least one more week.
>
> Reply with a 👍 if you're in, and tell us what you're bringing so we don't end up with 11 bowls of pasta salad. 🙏

## Shorter version

> WE'RE HOMEOWNERS 🏡🎉 Housewarming Sun Dec 7, 2-5pm at [address]. Potluck, so bring a dish. We'll supply drinks. Bring slippers, because the floors are freshly refinished! RSVP + tell us what you're bringing 🙌

## Why it's built this way

- **The "what to bring" ask is split into three lines.** Guests can skim it and still get the dish, drinks, and slippers right.
- **The slipper rule comes with a reason.** People follow "no shoes" more willingly when they know why, and the joke keeps it from sounding bossy.
- **Asking guests to say what they're bringing** works as a lightweight sign-up. You'll get a balanced spread without a spreadsheet.

## Optional follow-ups

**A week before:**
> One week until the housewarming! 🏡 Reminder: slippers or socks, and a dish to share. Anyone with allergies or dietary needs, tell me and I'll make sure there's something for you.

**Morning of:**
> Today's the day! 2-5pm, [address]. Parking: [tip]. Slippers + food, see you soon! 🧦🍲

Send me the address, the parking situation, and any dietary needs in the group, and I can fill those in.
